01 / NEW CHANNEL LAUNCH VISION

Ideation

NEW LAUNCH DIRECTION · OCTOBER 11

I Created the Multiverse

Alternate title: I Beat Minecraft With GTA. The Stokes crew uses GTA-style firepower and an Ender Dragon to survive a Minecraft world invaded by characters from other games.

Five thumbnail variants of one new episode. This is the user-selected first-video direction; the original 100-idea portfolio remains below.

A · Sky raidB · Hero chargeC · Last line of defenseD · Worlds collideE · The impossible ride
0 (First Frame)–5s

Open on the promised image: a Stokes host riding the Ender Dragon, firing down at a Flood creature, a zombie and a creeper in a bright Minecraft world.

5s–15s

I put all our favorite games into one world. We have to close these portals before they take over. Show the three portals, the crew and the shared life counter.

15s–30s

The first portal opens early: an ordinary Minecraft mob is followed by a creature that clearly does not belong. A crew member makes the first consequential rescue or mistake.

Why this idea, production and series

Why this idea

Shape: I Created ___ / I Beat ___ With ___. Ingredients: recognizable games, an impossible invasion, crew teamwork and a dragon-mounted finale.

I Created the Multiverse sells the universal spectacle; I Beat Minecraft With GTA names the collision and a clear win condition. The latter requires actual, recognizable GTA integration and a defensible definition of beating Minecraft. Do not count GTA-like generic guns alone as GTA or claim the normal dragon-kill ending while riding the only dragon without explaining a different final objective.

Working series through New Year

  1. Create the shared world and survive its first invasion
  2. Crew learns and exploits one new crossover mechanic
  3. A secret host-controlled escalation pranks the crew
  4. Risk a useful reward to unlock the next world
  5. End-of-year collective finale and meetup payoff, if confirmed

First few uploads build toward New Year; exact meetup payoff awaiting clarification. This is a working arc; the exact meetup payoff and episodes after the first remain open.

Prototype before expanding

One host and one crew client, one gun, one vehicle, one invasion enemy, one rideable dragon and a replayable 60-second encounter on one locked game version and loader.

Reuse the tested world, portal system, enemy waves and camera setup across later episodes; vary rules and cast roles before commissioning more worlds. The full compatibility stack, GTA-specific integration and production quote are unverified. Existing hardware is already available.

References

  • World's Largest Minecraft Build!: Observed thumbnail: large real host beside a block-built Earth with bright blue sky. Style/composition reference only; no claim this validates the new crossover.
  • Halo & MDE: Developer-maintained Halo mod listing. Candidate component, not a tested full crossover stack.
  • Dragon Mounts Remastered: Developer-maintained rideable dragon mod listing. Does not establish that the exact Ender Dragon and gun combination works.
  • Immersive Vehicles: Developer-maintained vehicle framework. Candidate tool, not evidence of GTA integration.

New user concept; no performance or compatible-modpack validation. Five thumbnails are variants of one episode, not five additional episodes.

Compare all five and leave shared team feedback ↗

20 formats. Five different videos in each. One collection of 100 finished thumbnail concepts.

Channel vision and working assumptions

The Stokes crew attempts extraordinary, easy-to-follow challenges inside games, with cinematic scale, personality, surprises and earned outcomes.

Largest worldwide audience pool; broadly understandable and recognizably Stokes.

Twins with cast and crew performing, cinematic gameplay and epic moments; presentation can evolve.

English first, designed for later localization.

GTA 5 is the launch foundation. GTA 6 is conditional on released capabilities; Minecraft and Roblox variations develop later. The twins anchor the brand while the full crew supplies choices, rivalry and comedy.

Real-city travel interpretation for the first three ideas; lower-cost across-game alternative also authored. Optional question remains unanswered.

Not committed; all cost ranges are planning allocations.

Twins and supporting crew available in principle; actual roster/time not booked.

Eight-upload proposed Nov–Dec calendar; original travel/approval conflicts not treated as completed.

Core directions retained by the user: 01, 02, 03, 06, 09, 12, 14, 15, 17, 18. Revised supporting formats are expanded under the full-document instruction; individual executions are creative proposals.

$1 vs $1,000,000 Cars in GTA

The crew races a wreck and an extravagant supercar through the same three tests to find what money really changes.

GTA 5 launch / follow-up · GTA 5

  1. 0 (First Frame)–5sA rusty tiny car left, a red supercar right, Alan between them; big $1 and $1M labels.

  3. 15s–30sThe cheap car stalls at the first start, so the crew has to decide whether the agreed retry rule applies. Show the crew choosing its next move.

Custom physics house and attachment system disclosed, active helicopter count verified and title revised to real achieved scale.

Escalation

One aircraft tips the load, a better rig balances it and the final team must coordinate a simultaneous ascent.

Payoff

Show the real lift or failure and the exact rig configuration responsible.

For both audiences

Gamer: Physics and mechanics reward prior knowledge.

Non-gamer: Scale and an intuitive question carry the suspense.

People and production

Crew teams propose and build different barriers; Alan/Alex or another host runs the test while participants react to the result.

Reusable custom challenge: $3,400–$7,500 incremental allowance. authored planning allowance; no vendor quote or approved funding

02 / NEW CHANNEL LAUNCH VISION

Packaging

Make a stranger understand the human promise before they recognize the game. Keep the game name as context, then earn the click with a familiar object, unequal stakes, an intriguing secret or a visible decision. The thumbnails carry cinematic scale; the page stays simple.

  • Expectation match: the opening gameplay must establish the same object, scale and danger shown in the thumbnail. Generated concepts are planning images; replace unsupported elements with the finished playable build before upload.
  • Complement the title: a price title gets a tangible cheap/expensive object, a secret-room title gets the entrance, and a risk title gets the visible thing that can be lost. Avoid pasting the complete headline into the image.
  • Use one dominant subject and at most three visual groups. A repeated wall of cars counts as one coherent group; ten disconnected props do not.
  • Recognizable Stokes face, expressive but story-appropriate emotion, photographic creator cutout and a coherent cinematic game world. Rotate who is featured when the crew member drives the story.
  • Show functional spectacle: a course has a reachable finish, a room has an entrance, a race has matching directions and a giant experiment has an observable impact. Increase actual consequence before increasing a title number.
  • At phone size, identify the face, challenge object and information gap in a glance. Preserve silhouettes, color separation and readable minimal labels; check the duration-overlay corner.
  • Translate later: ordinary words, numerals, objects and movement do the work. Avoid lore, unexplained acronyms, fake review screenshots and English puns as the sole hook.

SuperlativesMrBeast Gaming: World’s ___ median 0.83×, n=9; giant-experiment individual examples reach 2.78×/3.15×.Use verified spectacle and a simple experiment question; scale claims require a working prototype.

Testing the actual package

Create at least five distinct thumbnail sketches per pilot (comparison, action, reveal, scale, consequence), then choose one finished direction. This document supplies one selected concept per episode, not five rendered variants per idea. For upload tests, keep the premise truthful, compare watch-time share where native tests provide it, log dates and exposure, and avoid calling tiny uncontrolled samples winners.

The supplied thumbnail PDFs informed expectation match, one clear visual question, mobile readability, emotion and complementary title/image information. One rendered concept is supplied per episode. Make pilot variants before an actual upload test.

03 / NEW CHANNEL LAUNCH VISION

Creative

The broad audience watches a person attempt something clear; the gamer also enjoys the route, physics, build ingenuity or strategy. Introduce only the mechanic needed to understand the next consequence. A difficult game can hold a simple story.

HookHow to executeFormats
Visible mismatchStart with the wreck and supercar or the crew facing a hunter wall. A viewer can predict the obvious favorite before the first fair test.01, 02, 04
Physical questionPut the moving train and barrier in the same geography. Ask one concrete question, show the smallest failed test, then earn the bigger attempt.06, 09, 19
Dramatic ironyLet the audience see the hidden operator before the crew notices the obstruction. The gap is when and how the friends discover the cause.03, 07, 12
Immediate jeopardyShow the wave or locked exit while naming one attainable safe destination. Establish who can still succeed and what they carry.05, 14, 16
Meaningful choiceGive someone a reward they already care about, then offer one visible harder trial. Let the person deliberate instead of forcing a scripted risk.15, 17
Human wishRecord a friend’s exact wish before building. The payoff is their use and reaction, not an endless tour of expensive objects.08, 17, 20
Fair mysteryIntroduce a victim/object, suspects and one inspectable clue. Viewers should be able to form and revise an explanation.11
World comparisonUse a matched task/landmark in both worlds and an understandable finish. Their different constraints create the interest.10, 18
Comic competence gapShow a familiar job, a crew member’s bad first decision and its consequence. Their attempt to recover links the jokes into a story.13

Retentive story structure

StageEditorial purpose
0–30 secondsThe card’s three authored beats establish the image promise, objective/rule and first consequential attempt. No game-history lecture or obligatory cast roll call.
First actDemonstrate the minimum rules through a real attempt; show a failure that teaches viewers how success would work. Introduce personalities when their decisions matter.
MiddleEvery sequence changes state: route lost, reward banked, clue found, room discovered, supply saved, design improved. Alternate progress with setbacks; remove repeated resets without new learning.
Before finaleAccount for what remains and why the last attempt is harder or more meaningful. Re-establish geography and stakes so a casual viewer can follow the outcome.
FinaleResolve the actual challenge clearly, preserve the failure if that is what happened, then show the human reaction and fulfilled reward. No arbitrary extra twist after the main payoff.

Different ways to perform the content

  • Performed competition: a producer knows the rules, cast knows its role and the outcome remains earned. Use for races, pursuit, risk and obstacle attempts.
  • Authored environment with unscripted discovery: developers build the room/puzzle, audience sees selected clues, crew discovers it on camera. Use for secret rooms and prisons.
  • Performed story: clue logic, suspects and incident are authored; investigators and viewer deductions carry the mystery. Label clearly as a game-world story rather than a real crime.
  • Experiment documentary: predeclare conditions, preserve failures and show measured counts/settings. Cinematic replays clarify the result without replacing the test.
  • Crew comedy: normal job, meaningful score and recurring consequences. Plan playable situations rather than demand a joke at every cut.
  • IRL/game hybrid: match task scope, establish route and travel rules, capture both clocks. The differences between worlds are the entertainment, not a fairness issue hidden from viewers.

Cast and crew

Alan and Alex anchor recognition. Rotate operator, skeptic, ambitious builder, nervous driver, strategist, guest judge and comic challenger across the crew. Give a supporting performer the consequential choice or payoff when it improves the episode; use the twins’ relationship only when it adds a specific story beat.

Localization

Record clean isolated dialogue, protect words from music, keep names consistent, retain text-free title/thumbnail alternatives, export graphics separately and write jokes that survive translation. Explain a GTA wanted level as “the pursuers are closing in” before expecting the star icon to do the work. Teach a Minecraft interaction by showing its consequence.

Before greenlight, a non-gamer should explain the objective, failure condition and final reward from the first 30 seconds. A gamer should identify at least one real ingenuity or skill layer. This is a proposed editorial acceptance test, not measured audience retention.

04 / NEW CHANNEL LAUNCH VISION

Production

October 11 update: the Multiverse is now the first-video direction. The earlier eight-upload table below is a bank of options, not the final upload order. Prototype the crossover first, then choose low-cost follow-ups around its reusable world and the New Year payoff.

Budget the incremental work this episode causes: game systems, new builds, extra capture, edit complexity, travel and any real reward. Existing cameras, computers and regular cast/crew payroll are not repeatedly charged as new purchases. Their time still constrains the schedule.

All USD ranges are authored planning allowances, not vendor quotes or approved spending. Profiles separate per-video, one-time and monthly pools. They include incremental edit/capture allowances; replace them with actual internal capacity and quotes before booking. Real reward obligations are separate and are added only to funded variations.

How the format mix saves money

  • Light episodes: reuse a tested world, vehicles and scoring module. Batch myth attempts, prank triggers and price tests on one capture day while recording unique story outcomes.
  • Medium episodes: build one reusable pursuit, puzzle or course system; vary routes, goals and cast decisions. Prototype the highest-risk feature before spending on cinematic polish.
  • Heavy episodes: commission a scoped room, disaster or attraction build. Approve one working hero feature first, then add the supporting set. Empty visual scale is not enough.
  • Travel episodes: number of travelers, cities, nights and permitted activities drives cost. A local city pilot tests the hybrid before flights and hotels for a multi-city or global journey.
  • Prize episodes: virtual money is explicit. A real Lamborghini, million-dollar payment or unlimited purchase is not a launch expense assumption. Dinner for a year needs a funded meal allowance and exact terms.

Post-Production

Four real peer/main-channel videos were sent for automated footage analysis. The moment notes identify candidate hooks, reveals and decisions to inspect; they do not identify measured retention winners. Two analyses cover only introductory excerpts and one stops before the catalogue runtime. Source-linked timestamps make each observation reviewable.

No private YouTube Studio CTR, retention curves or audience-segment data has been supplied for Stokes Gaming or the parent channel. No MoreNizarisaqt graph is imported as Stokes evidence. Automated scene indexing can misdescribe longer videos; verify the original footage before copying an editorial moment.

Review the edit before upload

  • First-frame match: compare the thumbnail subject, opening environment and first spoken objective. Remove an unrelated cold open that postpones the promised challenge.
  • Geography: use a brief overhead/map when the viewer loses the destination, then return to character action. A string of close-up crashes cannot explain who is winning a chase.
  • State changes: annotate every new clue, decision, failure and gain. Cut repeated travel/reset footage when it changes neither understanding nor stakes.
  • Reactions: preserve the decision, consequence and response in order. Do not splice a different reaction onto the result for manufactured drama.
  • Payoffs: include the complete final attempt and real reward handoff. The viewer must know what happened before the cast celebrates.
  • Avoid: unexplained inventory jargon, repeated rule speeches, arbitrary difficulty without a goal, visually impressive builds that never function and expensive prizes that have no human decision attached.

Measure the channel’s actual learning

WhenMeasurement
Before launchCreate an event log keyed to source timecode: opening promise, first attempt, rule explanation, travel, reveal, choice, setback, finale and outro.
After each uploadWith authorized Studio access, export the real curve and align it to the event log. Inspect the first 30 seconds, exits around repeated explanations and responses to each payoff; watch the footage around every candidate dip/peak.
Compare fairlySeparate first-time and returning viewers where available, traffic sources, age of upload and video length. Lifetime public lift and retention percentage are different quantities.
DecideA spike may be replay/confusion and a dip may be skipped dead time. Record a hypothesis, make one clear editorial change in the next comparable episode and check the outcome.

Each episode handoff contains the raw camera/gameplay clocks, separate cast audio, working map/mod version, rule/trigger log, attempt log, true count/prize ledger, edit event sheet, clean graphics and delivery receipt for funded rewards. An editor can verify the ending without relying on a producer’s memory.

06 / NEW CHANNEL LAUNCH VISION

Shorts Strategy

Use standalone micro-stories that make a complete promise and show a result. Actual public Shorts examples below establish identifiable formats and raw reach, not a proven conversion system or age-controlled outlier lift. GTA myth examples come from two creators; Minecraft examples show a clear constraint and a hidden-build reveal.

For each long-form capture, deliberately record one self-contained myth test, one decisive crew reaction and one reveal or near-failure with enough vertical framing. Publish only clips with their own setup and payoff. Start with a small varied batch rather than filling a daily quota with incomplete teasers.

Working launch experiment: two strong Shorts around each of eight uploads, plus one native micro-experiment when capture capacity allows. Timing is a testable publishing plan, not an algorithm rule. Keep the long-form team’s edit bandwidth protected.

Reuse clip allowance: $60–$180 incremental edit/graphics per finished Short. Native capture allowance: $180–$650 plus $0–$300 of new game setup. These are authored planning ranges, exclude regular payroll already budgeted and do not add a duplicate charge when the same work is included in a long-form profile.

Attach the related long-form video where the platform permits and track engaged views, viewed-versus-swiped, actual retention, returning viewers and attributable long-form traffic with authorized analytics. A Short can have many public views and still attract viewers who never watch the launch channel’s episodes.

S01

One spectacular myth, complete verdict

A familiar-looking claim gets a decisive test.

Hook: Show the car or object poised for the unusual test and state the claim in plain words.

  • 0–2s: claim/object
  • 2–8s: conditions
  • 8–25s: actual attempt
  • 25–35s: result and one crew reaction

Need: Crop or recapture one complete long-form myth with a wide enough vertical frame.

Cost: Reuse: $60–$180 edit allowance; new capture $180–$650 plus only new setup.

Data Analysis

The research uses the public Influint intelligence index, gaming theory/standing/rejection pages and five public channel catalogues, plus exact primary video metadata and capability sources. Authenticated API/private creator data was unavailable. The plan uses the system’s evidence labels and keeps theory, observed performance and creative hypotheses separate.

MetricMeaning and boundary
Public individual liftInfluint reports views relative to publication-date nearby uploads. The exact neighbor count/value is not exposed. Preserve each row’s metric window; some displayed 28d labels conflict with the global lifetime description.
Repeated title familiesAll 23 displayed repeated Stokes/MrBeast Gaming family memberships were read; medians, sample size, date range, recent subsets, best and weakest examples were recomputed from reported lifts.
Outlier coverage2.0× is the declared qualifying threshold, with separate shape and ingredient matches. Adjacent examples, raw view counts and 1.97× secret-room evidence do not count as 2× proof.
Creator diversityTwo channels can belong to the same creator ecosystem: Preston/Brianna are grouped together. Count channels and creator groups separately.
FootageAutomated timestamps are qualitative candidate observations, with incomplete analysis scope disclosed. They are not Studio retention measurements.
Generated imagesOne independently generated selected concept per idea, exact prompt/reference IDs, image dimensions, hashes and recorded model availability. No image has a measured CTR result.
CostsIncremental USD planning assumptions, separate per-video/one-time/monthly pools and unfunded real-prize liabilities. No contractor quote or approved cash budget is implied.

Influint Intelligence applications

Applied labels retain their evidence standing. Near-duplicate gaming claims sometimes have conflicting Theory and Rejected labels; none of the six items below is presented as a universal law.

System topicStandingApplication / limit
Setup cost and viewsTheory / similar rejected entryUse cheap pilots to learn; the public system does not prove that setup cost is unrelated to views.
Three-to-five game roundsTheoryTest escalating rounds only when they earn different choices and a finale; treat exact timing as a proposal.
Novelty early, familiarity laterTheoryStart a distinct attempt early; confirm any benefit with the channel’s actual event log and curve.
Average view duration aloneWarningCompare percent viewed, length and moments; the niche evidence is limited and CTR is unavailable.
Audience-specific upload timingTheoryUse authorized audience-online data; public posting time does not establish an audience peak.
Manufactured winner attachmentTheory / contradictory rejected entryCapture real choices and reactions. Do not invent earlier testimony after learning the winner.
Intelligence indexGaming intelligenceEvidence system

Targets and tentative financial scenarios

The tentative PDF targets 10M subscribers and 10M first-28-day views per video by January 1, with overtaking MrBeast Gaming as an aspiration. These goals are not forecasts. The user’s working capacity is eight uploads, not ten.

ScenarioArithmetic / unvalidated assumption
Original per-video scenario22M main-channel views × 42% transfer = 9.24M gaming views. At assumed $7–$10 RPM: $64,680–$92,400; 25% production share: $16,170–$23,100. Arithmetic holds; transfer, views and RPM are unvalidated.
Exact 5% upkeep scenario722M × 5% = 36.1M monthly views, not 39M. At $7–$10 RPM: $252,700–$361,000; 10% upkeep: $25,270–$36,100.
Separate 39M upkeep scenario39M assumed monthly views gives $273,000–$390,000; 10% is $27,300–$39,000. Keep this as a different assumption. 195M / 3.71B ≈ 5.26%, not exactly 5%.
Timing and unitsThe first numerator models per-video first-28-day views, not monthly revenue. The PDF’s upkeep ceiling starts after six months. None of these scenarios authorizes launch spending.

What remains unknown

  • No authenticated API/private Studio data was queried.
  • Exact game-versus-IRL and GTA-city journey performance precedent remains unverified.
  • Per-episode gaps are enumerated; adjacent examples do not count as outlier replication.
  • Some view-window labels conflict with the global metric description.
  • Two Shorts shelf classifications are provisional; no conversion analytics.

Refresh public reference snapshots before selecting the next slate; preserve immutable snapshots and observed dates. Once the channel has comparable uploads and authorized analytics, build its own nearby-upload baseline rather than applying Stokes-main-channel views to a new gaming channel.

The two attached thumbnail PDFs informed expectation match, complementary text/visuals, one clear subject, restrained visual groups, mobile readability and appropriate emotion. Relevant frameworks include price/size comparison, action, hidden reveal, object repetition, landscape/map and transformation. Social/news UI is used only when it is genuine evidence; a decorative fake headline is not needed.
